text_simplified: The text speaks of an old story that shows the importance of tawakkul (reliance on Allah) together with taking the means. It relates that a man asked the Prophet ﷺ about leaving his son unsecured, so he ﷺ replied that one must first tie the camel, then rely on Allah. The story teaches us that planning and hard work do not conflict with trust in Allah.

review_defects.english: asked the Prophet ﷺ ... he ﷺ replied
review_defects.why: English adds the honorific ﷺ after 'the Prophet' and after the pronoun 'he', but the Arabic text does not include any honorific. This is an addition of religious attribution not present in the source.
Arabic specifies a female camel (she-camel), while English uses the generic 'camel', losing the gender distinction.
Arabic means 'without tying' (i.e., not tied up), but 'unsecured' is vague and could imply not made safe rather than specifically not tied.
The term 'tawakkul' is transliterated earlier in the text, but here it is translated as 'rely on Allah' instead of keeping the transliteration, creating inconsistency.
